cover: Checklist for reviewing an MCP connection

slides.title: Which AI tools will use it?
slides.body: Test the connection with the applications people plan to use, including their sign-in and permissions.

slides.title: Read before write
slides.body: A server that only reads orders shouldn't be able to cancel them. Start read-only, then add write tools one at a time.

slides.title: Where did the server come from?
slides.body: A local MCP server runs on your computer with your permissions. Install it like any software, from sources you trust.

slides.title: What will the AI read?
slides.body: An email or web page arriving through a tool can carry hidden instructions. Plan for that before you connect it.

slides.title: Who owns the agent's limits?
slides.body: Decide what it may do alone, what needs approval and what gets logged. Name an owner before exposing write tools.

slides.title: Is the API underneath good enough?
slides.body: An MCP server usually sits on an API you already have. If that API is thin or inconsistent, start there.
